# Current state

Updated 2026-11-08 (Pacific). The cross-shader/cross-machine screening audit is
complete. Supported targets are Complementary Reimagined, Complementary Unbound,
BSL and MakeUp Ultra Fast. The retention decision below supersedes earlier
shortlists and recommendations to continue screening these candidates.

## Latest outcome and next action

**Philip's retention decision, 2026-11-08 (Pacific): retain an optimization only
if it showed a positive result across all four supported shaders AND both
completed machines. None qualified. All sixteen candidates — G01–G10, C01–C02,
N01–N04 — are parked. No default enablement.** A held or unavailable cell is not
a positive result. Parking preserves implementations, reports, charts and all
other evidence; it does not erase scoped gains or claim universal impossibility.

The completed machines are Fedora Asahi Remix at 2560×1600 and native Windows
RTX 5080 / driver 617.42 at 3840×2160, with original shader settings and AA.
The Asahi audit classified 64 cells, 36 timed; the RTX audit has dispositions for
all 64 cells: 40 measured with two independent primary processes each, 22
source-held, and two shared G01 rows. Existing evidence remains authoritative:
[Asahi conclusions](../dev/experiments/asahi-four-target-audit-20261104/audit-conclusions.json),
[Asahi audit detail](STATUS_AUDIT_20261105.md) and
[RTX report and charts](../dev/experiments/rtx5080-four-target-audit-20261106/REPORT.md).
No new measurements accompany this decision. Percentages below are mean
frame-time reductions against matched controls; positive means faster.

Near-misses are **parked with reasons**, not retained winners:

- **MakeUp G01 copy omission:** about +8.14% on Asahi and +3.24% on RTX;
  replicated on both machines, but only MakeUp, with the other packs held.
- **C02 bloom VRS:** RTX BSL/Reimagined/Unbound +2.24%/+2.01%/+1.77%;
  MakeUp held. NVIDIA-only quality tradeoff, unavailable on Asahi because the
  required NV capabilities are absent; fails the all-shader/all-machine rule.
- **BSL G02 mip omission:** RTX BSL +3.95%, but Reimagined -5.67% and
  Unbound -10.01%; a BSL-only win that regresses Complementary.
- **MakeUp G06 exact AO attenuation:** about +4.14% repeated on Asahi;
  RTX MakeUp about +0.05% (~zero), with harmful results on the other packs.
  The Asahi-only gain does not qualify.

MakeUp N04's RTX +1.12% is sky-view-only and negative on the other packs;
MakeUp G04's +0.26% has the other packs held. G03/G05/G06/G07 and most other
measured RTX cells are slower or approximately zero. None changes the parking
decision. MakeUp G01/N02/N03 share one deletion result and must not be added
together; isolated effects from other routes must not be added either.

**Next useful engineering:** extend the existing measurement system into a
[cost map](COST_MAP.md) of named Iris passes, CPU work, GPU intervals and waits,
with native-pack baselines for all four targets on both machines and first-class
absent/enabled-DH cohorts, LOD CPU/GPU coverage and horizon scenes. Philip authorized stages 2–4 implementation and bounded Asahi end-to-end testing
on 2026-11-08 (“go build the whole thing and test it well e2e”). The section 10
capture program, RTX/Nsight calibration, training and stage 6 review remain unauthorized. The cost map should identify large slices to
investigate; the maintained A/B total-frame protocol remains the proof method.
Do not start another G-number optimization campaign from the parked shortlist.

**Cost-map stage 1 landed (2026-11-08):** development-only versioned event records,
integer scope registry, frame/epoch/graph/invocation ownership, explicit missingness
(including DH identity), bounded buffers and loss health. CPU-only synthetic checks
cover all eight stage-1 acceptance items; adjacent sampling-policy/statistics checks
also pass. No runtime timing or client was run. See the [stage-1 contract notes](COST_MAP_STAGE1.md)
for the test command and stage-2 seams. The subsequent [implementation checkpoint](COST_MAP_IMPLEMENTATION.md) adds timer/probe
lifecycle changes, optional canonical live-hook records, source seeds and an offline
export pipeline. Stages 2–4 are **partially implemented, not accepted complete**;
that note lists remaining authorized work. Stage-1 checks and synthetic pipeline
e2e pass. The follow-up now adds the owned live launcher, automatic graph/cohort
boundaries and physical DH joins. Bounded original-MakeUp runs on Apple M1 at
2560×1600 passed absent-DH and enabled-DH CPU/GPU hook/export checks, Iris reload,
and explicit DH rendering off/on transitions, with config/whole-save restoration.
The subsequent coverage follow-up adds task-owned DH generation/loading/
propagation/conversion hooks, CPU upload timings/bytes, real uploaded far-buffer
residency, saved horizon/water poses, workload requests and four-pack source/graph/
option semantic binding. MakeUp and BSL passed bounded live residency and new
collector checks; both Complementary originals failed enabled-DH composite1 linking
on Apple M1 (`Too many fragment shader texture samplers`). Their live mapping
cells are blocked after real attempts. Original settings/packs were preserved.
A generation-disabled request was exercised and restored; residual loading stayed
visible rather than being called a steady dataset. Conversion and DH shadows were
not exercised. A resource-identified DH depth handoff hook is implemented and CPU-tested;
its last live attempt was blocked by storage admission.
[Implementation and precise limits](COST_MAP_IMPLEMENTATION.md),
[coverage evidence](../dev/experiments/cost-map-coverage-20261108/RESULTS.json).
All-four-pack live acceptance and full stages 2–4 acceptance remain incomplete;
machine qualification remains unperformed. No optimization or later campaign ran.

## Completed audit context (2026-11-07)

The RTX audit retains nine original-only baseline cohorts with two independent
processes each: native 3.2 and real 4.6 for every pack, plus BSL's optimized-stack/
native cohort. Frame, window-mean and independent-process variance remain separate.
The G02 result above is the public singleton request, not the private prototype.

Windows sharing/recovery, C01 core polygon state, finite platform admission,
authored/resource/catalog drift, recipe pins and required-context failures were
repaired and validated on hardware. All eight focused Runtime-V4 checks and all24
affected comparisons/controls pass/restored. Extra4.6 G03 diagnostics remain6.99%
and10.81% slower on Reimagined/Unbound; native context did not explain the regression.
All572 valid measured windows pass the exploratory2% quarter/pair trend review,
without trimming samples. G06's extra full-size target/half viewport is intentional.
Source/work/JFR diagnosis does not establish hardware-optimal implementations or
isolate every CPU/GPU bottleneck.

Six motion checks retain2,178 complete lossless native/candidate/return images.
All frames were decoded/hashed and compared; reviewed overview/unscaled samples
show no gross defect. Shader clocks/history remain unmatched, so deterministic
pixel/HDR equivalence, brief temporal artifacts, all scenes/transitions and broad
DH/PBR compatibility remain unqualified. Earlier incomplete attempts stay invalid.
The recorder now holds its logical path for render/writer capacity, preserving
121-frame completeness without feeding capture stalls into timing data.

The final [terminal audit](../dev/experiments/rtx5080-four-target-audit-20261106/terminal-audit-v7.json)
verifies217 operations terminal/restored/released, both managed profiles matching
canonical inputs and zero Minecraft clients. The final owned scheduled task is
removed. Cleanup remained ShaderLOD-only with verified backups; the32GiB reserve
was preserved. [Artifact locations/recovery](../dev/experiments/rtx5080-four-target-audit-20261106/ARTIFACTS.md).
These completed screening and recovery records remain evidence; they do not
retain any candidate under the 2026-11-08 rule or authorize production engineering.

RTX2080Ti remains outside this allocation; renew availability before using it.
The active source branch is `rtx5080-audit`; milestone pushes go to user-owned origin.

## Find context

- [Benchmark guide](BENCHMARK.md) and [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md): maintained routes.
- [Experiment history](EXPERIMENTS.md): previous attempts, evidence and reasons to revisit.
- [Cost-map design sketch](COST_MAP.md): proposed measurement extension; no runtime validation yet.
- [Latest audit detail](STATUS_AUDIT_20261105.md) and [earlier campaign snapshot](STATUS_HISTORY_20261105.md): historical results/decisions.

At milestones update objective, latest meaningful result/limits, owner/run evidence
if active, and next action here. Link detailed records; do not copy every progress
update or old ownership statement into current state.

Record meaningful attempts rather than every monitoring update.

Search for relevant prior attempts before optimization work. Add a row for a meaningful result, not every run. Scope and evidence limit each result; a prior outcome does not prohibit a changed approach. Historical records were archived during the 2026-10-31 documentation cleanup at `/home/philip/shaderlod-doc-archive-20261031/docs-and-agent-setup.tar.gz`; this index is not yet exhaustive. **Current direction (2026-11-08 Pacific):** [STATUS](STATUS.md#latest-outcome-and-next-action)

shaders and both completed machines (Asahi and RTX 5080). None qualified;
G01–G10, C01–C02 and N01–N04 are all parked, with no default enablement.
Historical gains, implementations and evidence remain preserved. The next useful
engineering direction is the [cost-map extension sketch](COST_MAP.md), not more
G-number optimizations. This documentation decision adds no measurements.

**Historical campaign disposition (2026-11-01; superseded as current direction):** the user resumed sustained optimization/review, excluding C02. # Benchmark guide

For the local Asahi machine without a desktop, see [headless development](HEADLESS.md).
The maintained Linux ARM64 launcher selects its installed GPU-backed virtual
display when no display is explicitly selected; the native 2560×1600 viewport
and all normal benchmark guards remain required.

For the prepared RTX 2080 Ti Windows host, see [Windows benchmarking](WINDOWS_BENCHMARK.md).

Use the maintained command for discovery, planning, execution and results:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py discover
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py baseline --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --output FRESH_BASELINE
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py plan --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py check --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_CHECK_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py report --output REPORT
```

`discover` lists local managed slots, worlds and shader archives. It is an inventory, not compatibility approval. Use `--profile` instead of `--slot` for an explicit prepared client. Set `--width` and `--height` to the intended native viewport (the local Asahi fullscreen mode is 2560×1600). Select the exact original pack/options for the feature; private candidates use `--candidate` instead of `--feature`. See the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md) for specialized scenes, compatibility checks and qualification protocols.

`baseline` renders the original pack with the main mod absent in the backed-up
authored save. After 120 seconds conditioning it captures three unchanged
20-second native windows, with the standard ownership, readiness, sample and
restoration checks. The report gives frame sample variance/SD (ms²/ms), and
separately variance/SD of the three window means and first-to-last drift.
These describe frame jitter and within-process variation, respectively; neither
is a confidence interval. Repeat in fresh processes to measure between-run
variation. Keep absent-mod baselines separate from the matched Master-Off
controls in optimization comparisons. Startup failure supplies no frame-time
measurement. `native-startup` remains a short original-only startup diagnostic.

`--gl-context native` preserves Minecraft's normal context request. For explicit
desktop API coverage, maintained comparisons also accept `3.2`, `4.3`, `4.5` and
`4.6`. These request real GLFW contexts; they do not override reported versions
or capabilities. Explicit requests disable NeoForge's reusable early window in
the owned profile, with the normal configuration backup/CAS/restoration contract.
The returned desktop version must meet the requested minimum and is recorded in
`summary.json.gl_context`. A driver returning4.6 for a4.5 request is labeled4.6;
it does not supply an independent4.5 result. Keep actual context/configuration
cohorts and their native baselines separate. Frozen Bliss qualification retains
its existing native-context protocol and refuses an explicit context override.
`--expected-renderer 'RTX 5080'` additionally refuses a ready client on a different
GPU, including a hardware integrated GPU. It validates the observed renderer
before scoring; it does not select the GPU or change personal driver settings.

`--performance-stack optimized` selects the exact pinned ModernFix, FerriteCore
and ImmediatelyFast tuple for G03 and its matched original-only startup/baselines or byte-identical native controls.
Default remains `minimal`. Other private/frozen protocols reject this override.
Preflight verifies every optional JAR, launch uses the maintained stack selector,
and runtime readiness checks the actual loaded module versions before scoring.
Optional artifacts are frozen operation inputs. Keep stack cohorts separate;
selecting the tuple is not proof that G03 compiled, executed, or helped.

`plan` runs the standard test's static checks without compiling, launching or creating the report. It lists the resolved launch plan, schedule, per-check elapsed time, failures and remedies. A stale build is reported; `test` rebuilds it automatically before launch. Native options and canonical profile inputs are checked; preserve unexplained differences before resetting a managed slot. Runtime-only checks still run in the client.

`check` accepts the same candidate arguments and exercises activation, available source/work checks, short captures and restoration without the two-minute conditioning period. It reports no performance or visual qualification. Use it when checking whether a newly integrated candidate runs; use `test` for a development performance comparison. Frozen Bliss qualification cannot use `check`.

`test` uses the fixed native/candidate/native-return protocol described below. `report` reads existing reports without launching anything, including historical reports. Its decision gives drift comparison precedence over an averaged positive mean, and identifies invalid runs or recovery requirements. It does not grant optimization closure or compatibility qualification. Phase timings in `summary.json` include nested profile preparation/restoration details; do not sum nested details into the total again.

Windows ownership JSON reads and atomic publication retry transient sharing errors
for at most three seconds, including CRT EACCES/EPERM errors that lack a Windows
error number; persistent denial still fails the operation. Normal
configuration restoration includes the five numbered FML backups for each
ShaderLOD client config. For an older interrupted report that omitted these
paths, `recover --output REPORT --preserve-generated-backups` retains newly
created known backups in that report before checking the complete original
profile map. Existing backups and unknown files retain normal ownership checks;
recovery never replays measurements.

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

The command automatically selects the existing Linux ARM64 launcher on that platform. Explicit `linux_arm64_runtime.py` commands remain supported. It finds an installed full JDK21 or a cached Gradle JDK21; an explicit JAVA_HOME retains precedence. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

C02 is an explicitly labeled 2×2 bloom quality tradeoff, with Master-On native
controls; its scoped exception is documented in the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md#c02-experimental-bloom-shading-rate).

## Choose the check for the question

| Question | Maintained route | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What inputs and candidates exist? | `discover`, then `plan` with selected inputs | Runtime compatibility or ownership |
| Does this change activate and recover? | `check` | Performance or visual equivalence |
| Is the idea worth more investigation? | `test`, then `report` | Broad workload/machine qualification |
| What does native do without ShaderLOD? | `baseline` | Installed-Off overhead by itself |
| Does it preserve motion or work across packs/hardware? | Candidate-specific protocols in the reference | Coverage of untested scenes, transitions or machines |

Before designing a new study, establish the user's intended decision: deep
workload performance, compatibility breadth, quality, or a quick screen. Reuse
the supported commands above. Put the chosen claim, comparator, coverage, useful
metrics, controls and budget in the existing experiment record. Record exclusions
and fallback separately; do not impose a universal repetition count or payback
horizon. Performance requires actual-window execution and valid output evidence,
not merely enabling a setting. Source changes do not inherit earlier timings.

## Records and milestone cleanup

Keep current work in STATUS, durable attempts/decisions in EXPERIMENTS, supported
procedures here and specialized routes in BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES. Extend the existing
candidate entry when adding a route; retire superseded wrappers only after checking
imports, tests and historical reproduction dependencies. Keep active experiments in
`dev/experiments`, reusable inputs/clients in `dependencies` and `run-workloads`,
and retained historical evidence in `experiment-evidence`. Do not move a pinned
active path just to satisfy this layout.

After an investigation, preserve compact raw measurements, configuration/source
identity, conclusions and any images/motion needed to support the claim. Remove
owned disposable intermediates once dependencies and restoration are checked;
there is no background cleanup requirement. For old camera sequences, put a
nonempty `.storage-retire` file beside the frames only after recording the reason
and retained evidence location. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py prune-captures`

checks. Age alone is not permission to discard motion evidence. `.storage-keep`
on an ancestor protects a subtree. Unknown or still-needed evidence stays intact.


## Cost-map diagnostic checkpoint

Offline commands never launch a client; live diagnostics stay outside scored A/B:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py profile-plan --fps 60 --seconds 20 --windows 3 --processes 2 --cadence 4 --scope-sets 7
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py profile --input /absolute/path/capture.json --output /absolute/path/new-report
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py profile-report --input /absolute/path/capture.json --output /absolute/path/new-report
```

`profile --input` imports an existing schema-1 canonical cohort.
`profile --live --profile MANAGED_CLIENT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --seconds 8 --output FRESH`
launches an owned native 2560×1600 Asahi client in the prepared authored save,
captures CPU/GPU records, exercises an Iris reload, exports each cohort and restores
configuration and the whole save. Capture duration is bounded to 1–30 seconds;
startup/world loading are separate bounded phases. `--dh` enables pinned owned JAR
staging; `--dh-transition-check` explicitly tests rendering off/on with API override
restoration. Generation/radius/mode/distance remain the existing effective inputs unless the
explicit steady workload request described below owns generation=false.
The report is diagnostic, not an A/B performance or readiness qualification.
`profile-report` regenerates offline exports. Output must
be a new directory; existing finalized output is never overwritten. Legacy
unversioned `report.json` is read and labeled duration-only without inventing
endpoints. `profile-plan` estimates regularly active observations per scope set
using `floor(fps * seconds * windows * processes / cadence / scope_sets)` and exits
1 below `--minimum` (default 100). It does not inspect a live slot or qualify overhead.

CSV/JSON/HTML and separate CPU/GPU trace exports preserve missing values. Elapsed
GPU data has no timeline positions; uncorrelated GPU timestamps never share a CPU
trace. Cost labels and inclusive hierarchy are nonadditive. See
[COST_MAP_IMPLEMENTATION](COST_MAP_IMPLEMENTATION.md) for exact implemented scope,
test evidence and remaining stage 2–4 work. No four-pack capture study is implied.


Cost-map live coverage additions (2026-11-08): `--scene horizon` and `--scene water`
select saved poses 12/13 in the same authored world and retain a separate native
screenshot before timers start. `--workload steady` explicitly owns a temporary
DH generation=false API override and restores the prior API value (including
absence); it does not guarantee queues have drained. `--workload streaming`
labels the request without clearing caches, moving the camera or enabling generation.
The default `observed` preserves the generation policy. Reports distinguish the
request from actual task/queue evidence; loading during a steady request stays
visible. Generation-disabled rendering cannot establish generation cost.

`task-costs.csv` reports CPU wall/thread task distributions; `dh-tasks.csv` retains
individual intervals, thread identities, failures and requested upload bytes.
Tasks are window-owned and nonadditive with render-frame scopes. Readiness uses
fresh world-list uploaded VBO containers wholly beyond the vanilla distance square,
not submissions alone. It establishes residency, not visible pixels or complete
horizon coverage. Four-pack mixed labels and limits: [DH catalog](COST_MAP_DH_CATALOG.md).

# Candidate and qualification reference

Shared private prototypes are registered once in `PRIVATE_CANDIDATES` in `scripts/run_benchmark.py`: validator/producer module, report key, and whether a settled observation is required. The parser, launch hooks and common observation lifecycle use that definition. Modules retain their exact input admission, staging, activation, source/work validation and assessment. Specialized routes outside this lifecycle retain their existing handlers.

`--candidate native-control` is a known-null control for maintained original
adapters. B is a byte-identical ZIP alias with the same native options, Master
Off and no public requests. Actual linked source, directives and logical image
read/write/copy signatures must agree across arms. It measures reload/session
noise, never optimization benefit; `check` is functional only. This general
control does not replace or relax the separately frozen Bliss qualification.

For public comparisons or `native-control`, `--comparison-order ABBA|BAAB`
selects four standard-duration windows: A native Off, B candidate. Both orders
balance a linear time trend; neither removes nonlinear drift or thermal effects.
The report separates frame variance from the variance of the two window means
per treatment. Repeat in fresh processes for between-run variation. An explicit
untimed return to original selection, Master Off and empty requests follows the
fourth window. Other private candidates retain their established schedules.

`--audit-graph` exports the selected graph, linked program inventory and active
scalar controls after each comparison arm, outside timing. The generic public
`--untimed-diagnostic selected-work` additionally uses the existing two-frame
source/physical observation and a next-frame reset after an untimed reload.
Returned draws and live controls do not count avoided fragments or samples.
The observer is disarmed before further timing. `g02-family` retains its separate
executed-mip omission checks.

The development runtime corrects Iris's sampler index budget to the lesser of
the combined texture-unit namespace and Minecraft's tracked texture-state
array. Shader linking still enforces per-stage sampler resource limits, and
Iris allocation and cleanup use the same bound. This preserves original packs,
options and AA. On Asahi, the old fragment-count budget exhausted after reserved
unit holes despite 15 active samplers fitting the 16-sampler stage limit;
the repaired Complementary graph successfully uses binding index16. Treat
measurements before and after this correction as separate runtime cohorts.

Shared private runs use one atomic selection/source-observation reload per arm under an explicit `privateObservedReload` launch capability, with master Off, empty requests/options, actual dimension and archive-byte checks. Observers are disarmed before capture; the source/physical validators and native options remain required. Frozen Bliss qualification retains its separate launch gate and schedule. Historical multi-reload results remain separate evidence.

For the separately authorized frozen Bliss AO qualification, `test --candidate n04-bliss-sky --scene saved --saved-pose 0|7 --bliss-qualification null|clock|ao --qualification-order ABBA|BAAB` selects a maintained four-window block. A is the original; B is a byte-identical original ZIP alias for `null`/`clock`, or the existing AO candidate for `ao`. Current `atomic-observed-reload-v3` arms actual-source observation before the verified selected-pack reload in one owned action. Every arm drains prior GL work during untimed setup, then performs one successful-path reload; a failed reload disarms observation before rollback. This is a resource-peak experiment, not demonstrated memory reclamation. The earlier two-reload cohorts remain separate evidence. Timing is 60 seconds per window after 20 seconds settling, with initial 180-second conditioning and an 1800-second recovery-inclusive budget. Work counters are disabled; complete observer status must remain false at both timing boundaries. Strict checks reconcile contiguous single-epoch raw samples, render/world-entry counts, duration and returned-render timestamps. Start/render/end duration reconciliation permits a fixed 5ms difference between first/last endpoint bookkeeping. This measures total-frame start intervals, not GPU completion. `clock` declares a 25ms render-thread spin in B only; CPU/GPU overlap can hide some of that added CPU work in total throughput, so it is an instrument check, not an optimization or bandwidth result.

The bounded calibration and decision rules are frozen before runtime in `dev/experiments/benchmark-trust-bliss-20261103/preregistered-plan.json`: two clock blocks, then six fresh-process null blocks per scene with balanced orders; AO is gated on both scenes calibrating. All valid losses and invalid attempts remain recorded. `python3 scripts/benchmark_bliss_qualification.py --mode null|ao --runs /path/to/attempt ... --output /path/to/fresh/cohort.json` evaluates complete cohorts; AO additionally requires `--calibration /path/to/passing-null-cohort.json`. Uncertainty uses process blocks rather than individual frames, and remains approximate/session-specific. Single-block reports deliberately issue no performance qualification verdict. This protocol does not change prior goal dispositions or grant public/default, visual, DH/PBR or hardware-wide qualification.

The initial twelve-block Bliss null cohort failed calibration in both scenes; valid execution did not establish stable measurements. Both bounded repair cohorts remain incomplete after owned kernel OOM kills; v3 also contains a same-treatment spread above the original limit. The excluded capacity diagnostic is not a passing null cohort. See `dev/experiments/benchmark-trust-bliss-20261103/final-interpretation.json`; AO timing remains blocked. The prospective Linux memory-budget variant adds `--qualification-client-heap 1536m` (2304m is also explicitly supported). This changes only the owned client’s launch property, retains the existing Gradle budget and native shader quality, and verifies the effective JVM maximum before conditioning and at capture boundaries. Read-only host pressure/swap counters and client faults/RSS are sampled outside scored intervals; their external brackets include controller/export endpoints and do not isolate GPU or client causes. Source/runtime signatures prevent mixing heaps or instrumentation variants within a cohort or between passing null and AO cohorts. The separately frozen `preregistered-memory-repair-v2.json` defines one diagnostic and one replacement null cohort with unchanged acceptance gates. Swap occupancy, later quiet-host snapshots and a lower requested heap do not by themselves prove active swapping, reduced residency or the cause of prior stalls.

`--untimed-diagnostic cpu-admission-cost` requires the exact public CPU triple `--features quad_command_compaction,shadow_admission_cache,index_scalar_cache`, no DH, and a standard test. It observes at least128 completed frames after candidate timing, at the actual consumer checks and compactor/scalar bodies, inclusive native fill/maximum-query scopes, and nonshadow native submission delegate. It also measures4096 empty clock pairs once when arming. Nested/inclusive intervals must not be summed; scalar lifecycle includes eligible enter/finish plus all clear-site begin-selection callbacks, so it cannot be subtracted from fill. Native submission is CPU delegate-chain time, not GPU completion or isolated driver work. Clock aggregates include observer overhead; empty calibration is contextual and must not be blindly subtracted. Clock reads are disarmed in scored windows, while ordinary plans disable the diagnostic branch. Own-JVM DH-permission transitions test cache invalidation and restore every property; without DH installed they do not qualify live-DH admission. No consumer permission is reused or safety guard removed.

If the harness or inputs fail, preserve the failure, restore/release owned resources, fix the maintained harness or inputs, and retry. Do not copy harness code into report-local callers, inject launcher overrides, relax admission after failure, or substitute custom scripts for the standard result. Diagnostics are diagnostic and do not replace it. One Linux ARM64 BSL standard run completed with verified restoration and independent review; this does not establish behavior for other configurations or future changes. See [experiment history](EXPERIMENTS.md).

Keep reports, worlds, downloads, builds and captures out of Git. Do not kill unrelated processes. If restoration refuses due to unknown changes, preserve the data and inspect ownership and recovery before acting.

Runtime dependencies and original shader-pack inputs are stored under `dependencies/`. Keep active experiment output in `dev/experiments/` and any retained evidence in `experiment-evidence/`; both are local and outside Git. Prepared clients and worlds remain under `run-workloads/`.

## C02: experimental bloom shading rate

`--candidate c02-bloom-vrs` tests the existing NV shading-rate runtime on the
pinned original BSL10.1.8/native384 or Complementary Reimagined/Unbound5.9.3
with their exact non-PBR native398 options and a saved Overworld pose. Only the
owned composite4 bloom output is admitted: BSL target1 or Complementary target3.
Source/archive/native options and the declared single-output contract must match. No other feature requests or DH are accepted. This is an
explicit **quality tradeoff**: 2×2 bloom-prefilter shading, not image equivalence;
include it only when that scope is authorized. Native options and AA remain
required. Hardware/context, original selection and actual executed/restored
VRS draw checks can refuse the comparison; refusal is not zero speedup.

This candidate uses Master On with no public feature requests for both native
controls, and toggles only the experimental VRS request for its candidate arm.
The initial conditioning and standard capture durations are unchanged. The
harness disables the request before exit and restores the owned configuration.
See [Windows benchmarking](WINDOWS_BENCHMARK.md) for the prepared host.

`check --quality-motion` records a separate untimed native/candidate/native camera
sequence through the existing bounded lossless recorder. Public routes and the
qualified bloom-only C02 route are supported. It requires a
public saved-scene check without DH or balanced timing. Each arm warms for30s,
then follows the same20s eased path at six native-resolution PNG samples/second;
world day/weather stay frozen while Iris animation and temporal history advance.
PNG transport uses lossless zlib level0 and flushes each image's contents on the
writer thread before completion to avoid accumulating a large dirty-file backlog.
Level1 exceeded the single writer's CPU budget at native resolution on M1.
Actual camera poses, loaded inputs, file hashes and image-lease accounting are
retained. Any missing capture slot makes the sequence incomplete. This sampling
can reveal persistent ghosting, shimmer and abrupt changes; it does not establish
frame-by-frame temporal equivalence or acceptance of every LOD transition.

The quality-only launch flag is absent from scored comparisons. PNG readback and
writing can stall rendering, so its short functional windows are never scored as
performance evidence. The explicit output/capture cap is12GiB with the usual32GiB
free-space reserve; ordinary benchmark caps remain unchanged. Image leases must
drain before configuration edits, timing or restoration. The live storage census
records files that disappear during atomic publication and retries their final
names on the next scan; copy, symlink and ownership/CAS checks remain strict.

The untimed selected-work observer inventories all active scalar `shaderlod*`
uniforms at its draw boundary, including implementation permission uniforms.
Public request flags alone do not prove that a qualified branch saves work.

# Headless development on the Asahi host

The host runs without SDDM or the Plasma desktop. Minecraft still needs a display
server. `shaderlod-display.service` supplies a private KWin virtual output and
Xwayland, using the Apple M1 GPU at 2560×1600, scale 1. It does not depend on the
physical panel or lid state. This is a different presentation backend from the
old desktop; do not pool its timing results with old desktop measurements.

The service uses its own D-Bus session and configuration under
`~/.local/share/shaderlod-display/`. It does not load the Plasma workspace or
change personal desktop settings. Its environment file is private, lives under
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/shaderlod-display/`, and is checked against the current service
invocation. Readiness rejects software GL rendering and incorrect resolution.

## Normal use

Use the commands in [the benchmark guide](BENCHMARK.md). On Linux ARM64,
`run_benchmark.py test`, `check`, and `native-startup` automatically start and
select the installed headless service if neither DISPLAY nor WAYLAND_DISPLAY is
set. `plan`, discovery, report, build, and recovery do not start it. An explicitly
selected desktop display takes precedence.

For interactive development launches, use `scripts/linux_arm64_runtime.py client
on|off` with the ordinary `dev_client.py` arguments. This also selects the

runtime-validated.** This expands the existing cost-map sketch in place. No
Minecraft client, benchmark, GPU workload, Nsight capture or training was run to
prepare it. Research comprised repository/source inspection and primary profiler
documentation. All overhead numbers below are proposed acceptance budgets, not
measurements. The same-day Sol source review identified missing DH identity,
worker/upload boundaries, stage joins, horizon scenes, sample feasibility,
lifecycle invalidation and a selectable DH report. This revision incorporates
those findings; it does not establish implementation or live DH coverage.

[STATUS](STATUS.md#latest-outcome-and-next-action) owns current direction, allocation
and retention decisions. [BENCHMARK](BENCHMARK.md) owns supported commands and
performance proof. This document owns the proposed profiling design; proposed
commands here are not operational instructions. On implementation, document the
supported interface in BENCHMARK rather than maintaining two command guides.

## 1. Recommendation for Philip

Build a **development-only cost map**, extending `BottleneckProbe`, `GpuTimers`,
`CpuTimers` and their existing Iris/Sodium/DH hooks. Expose it as a separate
`profile` mode in the maintained benchmark harness, with its own capture ownership
and reports. Use a simple offline report for decisions and an exportable trace for
investigation. Do not put detailed profiling inside normal scored A/B windows.

The first screen should answer: **which named stages cost the most, what features
do they contain, how repeatable is that cost, and what remains unknown?** Philip
should be able to expand “shadows,” “fog,” “terrain,” or “post-processing” into
actual passes and submission work, select an area for investigation, and see the
same categories across the four packs. **Distant Horizons is a v1 measurement
target**, alongside vanilla terrain: both absent-DH and enabled-DH cohorts, CPU
LOD work, GPU draws, shadows and shader-pack consumers must be visible. DH is not
merely a later compatibility checkbox. A cost map is a way to choose work, not an
automatic optimization selector or evidence of an achievable speedup.

Provide three related views with explicit units and denominators:

- **Frame pacing:** total frame-start intervals, their distribution and variation.
- **CPU:** render-thread wall intervals, thread CPU consumption, known blocking
  calls and unattributed off-CPU time; optional sampled worker/JVM detail.
- **GPU:** measured command-stream elapsed intervals by named stage/pass/draw
  group, with feature labels, missing coverage and sampling uncertainty.

Do not promise an additive “CPU + GPU + wait = frame” chart. CPU submission and
GPU execution overlap and can cross frame boundaries. OpenGL timers do not expose
hardware busy time, all queues, occupancy, instruction cost or the critical path.
A shader function inside a mixed pass is not separately timed just because it has
a recognizable name.

This serves the decision after the completed 16-candidate screen: G01–G10,
C01–C02 and N01–N04 remain parked. There is no new optimization in this plan.
The native RTX 5080 baselines were already approximately 2.02–3.38 ms/frame;
small absolute observer costs matter. Reuse the completed [RTX report](../dev/experiments/rtx5080-four-target-audit-20261106/REPORT.md)
and [Asahi conclusions](../dev/experiments/asahi-four-target-audit-20261104/audit-conclusions.json)
as context, not pass measurements they never collected. Current STATUS supersedes
historical recommendations in those records.

The [current API matrix](https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-graphics/UserGuide/appendix.html) lists OpenGL GPU Trace but not OpenGL shader profiling. Historical range functionality is not a promise that an old release supports Blackwell. No Nsight Graphics capture on Asahi. |
| **Nsight Systems:** [OpenGL trace](https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-systems/UserGuide/index.html#opengl-trace) | Correlates CPU API calls, scheduling and GPU workload; exposes swap and synchronization behavior. Its OpenGL workload trace batches calls using timestamps, and debug ranges report incremental cost that does not fully represent overlapping draws. | Use on RTX for CPU/driver/queue/wait questions when supported, separately from Graphics hardware counters. Even an external trace has semantic limits; its GL ranges are not an unquestionable busy-time oracle. |
| **AMD Radeon GPU Profiler:** [events](https://gpuopen.com/manuals/rgp_manual/events_windows/), [queue timing](https://gpuopen.com/manuals/rgp_manual/overview_windows/), [requirements](https://gpuopen.com/rgp/) | Hierarchical user events, consistent marker colors, wave occupancy, barriers and submit/enqueue/execute distinctions explain why “long range” does not mean “shader arithmetic.” | Design reference. Current graphics support is DX12/Vulkan on supported AMD hardware, not this Iris/OpenGL workload or either allocated GPU. Do not add an AMD dependency or infer AMD compatibility. |
| **Microsoft PIX:** [Timing Captures](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/pix/timing-captures-new/), [GPU Captures](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/pix/gpu-captures/) | Timing captures preserve live CPU/GPU relationships. GPU replay distinguishes execution duration from end-of-pipe duration and may serialize queues that overlapped in the game. Named markers connect overview to individual actions. | Design reference for lanes, parent/child ranges and replay warnings. PIX GPU captures target D3D12, not native Iris/OpenGL. Do not port or translate the renderer to obtain a profile. |
| **RenderDoc:** [counter viewer](https://github.com/baldurk/renderdoc/blob/v1.x/docs/window/performance_counter_viewer.rst), [replay tradeoffs](https://github.com/baldurk/renderdoc/blob/v1.x/docs/how/how_control_replay.rst) | Event/resource inspection is valuable for understanding which draw produced an image; available counters can identify expensive captured events. Replay changes execution conditions. | Optional graph/resource verification if the exact driver supports capture. Not the main live frame profiler, CPU-wait tool or proof of original frame throughput. Counter availability is backend-dependent. |
| **Tracy:** [project](https://github.com/wolfpld/tracy), [OpenGL implementation](https://github.com/wolfpld/tracy/blob/master/public/tracy/TracyOpenGL.hpp) | Instrumented CPU/GPU zones, frame association and delayed query collection provide an approachable model. Its GL calibration code illustrates that correlation can introduce synchronization. | Borrow zone identity and on-demand capture ideas. Do not replace the Java timers with a new JNI/native profiler dependency in v1, or import synchronizing calibration into measured windows. |
| **Superluminal:** [sampling and instrumentation](https://superluminal.eu/docs/documentation.html) | Sampled stacks find costs outside anticipated scopes. Executing, waiting and unattributed time remain distinct, with inclusive/exclusive views. | Optional Windows native/driver CPU investigation. Java symbol/JIT visibility must be verified; do not promise it from native stack support. Its sampling rate is not an appropriate default to copy blindly. |
| **JFR/JDK Mission Control and async-profiler:** [JFR overhead](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/troubleshoot/troubleshoot-performance-issues-using-jfr.html), [async-profiler modes](https://github.com/async-profiler/async-profiler/blob/master/docs/ProfilingModes.md), [platforms](https://github.com/async-profiler/async-profiler) | JFR provides execution samples, GC/JIT and thresholded wait events. async-profiler separates CPU and wall sampling and includes Java/native stacks. Sample shares and wall durations answer different questions. | Reuse JFR analysis for separate untimed diagnosis. async-profiler is a later optional Linux arm64 path after permission/JVM checks; maintained platforms listed are Linux/macOS, not native Windows. Neither yields GPU percentages. Published JFR overhead is not ShaderLOD calibration. |
| **Apple Instruments / Metal System Trace:** [Metal tools](https://developer.apple.com/metal/tools/), [timestamp conversion](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/converting-gpu-timestamps-into-cpu-time) | Parallel CPU/GPU timelines, encoder labels and explicit timestamp correlation show the desired relationship between named work and hardware execution. | Reference for presentation and occasional separately scoped macOS/Metal investigation only. Fedora Asahi OpenGL is not a Metal application; macOS measurements cannot validate this Linux stack. |
| **gpuvis / Linux tracing:** [overview](https://github.com/mikesart/gpuvis/wiki/Overview), [Mesa Asahi](https://docs.mesa3d.org/drivers/asahi.html) | ftrace events and markers can connect scheduling, presentation and GPU activity where driver tracepoints exist. | Optional Asahi investigation after checking the actual kernel/Mesa event coverage and permissions. A GPU trace viewer does not create missing Asahi events. Mesa's documented macOS reverse-engineering wrapper is not a ready Linux frame profiler. |
| **Perfetto:** [track events](https://perfetto.dev/docs/instrumentation/track-events), [clock domains](https://perfetto.dev/docs/concepts/clock-sync) | Separate tracks for parallel work, nested slices for sequential scopes, counters/flows, and explicit clock correlation. | Preferred interoperable trace destination alongside a small offline report. An exported trace is visualization, not additional measurement. Uncorrelated clocks must not appear synchronized merely because a viewer uses one ruler. |

The common lesson: overview first, exact named scope next, deeper capture only
when needed. Hardware traces and sampled stacks complement lightweight ranges.
They do not justify attributing every millisecond to a feature or multiplying a
pass-time reduction into an expected FPS improvement.

The inspected NeoForge integration is not a replacement DH renderer.

pipeline, camera/travel and dimension changes. **Keep that policy inactive during
native cost mapping**; observing readiness does not authorize reducing vanilla
terrain. Its checks do not prove distant pixels or complete replacement coverage.
The Fabric/port `DhTerrainInputs` adapters are pinned optional API readers, not
proof that the current NeoForge timing mixins cover those loaders/versions.

recognizes only observed beacon cooldown sleeps; it neither hides all file work
